baseline_pass_mechanism: Preflight run 20260930-105529 (opus[1m], xhigh, k=3, 40 turns, main checkout evals/results/.../20260930-105529/transcripts/trial-{1,2,3}.txt): all three baseline trials took the same route. Each started with `find .`, and each made `cat maintaining-obsidian/references/audit.md` its second call. The script runs followed: trial 1 at call 7 (`python3 lint_vault.py ../../vault --field-empty-pct 90 --undeclared-pct 80 --tag-min 10 --title-match 0.8 --json`), trial 2 at call 6 (`--help && run`), trial 3 at call 5. Every trial then recomputed the sha256 by hand, grepped for Runbook-Legacy, wrote _audits/, and scored 1 on all ten assertions (grading/trial-*.json score 1). The baseline did not find the behavior on its own. The fixture gave it to the baseline three ways: (1) the Context named ./maintaining-obsidian/references as the skill's reference copy; (2) the prompt said `audit lint`, which is how audit.md's first line says to invoke it; (3) audit.md's LINT section has the run line with exactly the vault's numbers (90/80/10/0.8), and SCHEMA.md also spelled those as flags. So both arms read the instruction under test, and the arms differed only by SKILL.md, which audit.md restates.
new_trap: Version 3 measures a missing step, behind a shortcut that looks sufficient. The prompt is a plain request ("give the ops vault a health check and tell me what's wrong with it; don't fix anything yet"). It does not say audit or lint, and the Context no longer mentions the reference copy. SCHEMA.md's ## Audit Thresholds now states the four thresholds in prose, with no flag names. That matches the minimal preset, which ships that section as a TODO for the owner to fill. The values are 85/75/5/0.9, which differ from audit.md's example values, so pasting the example no longer passes. Baseline-failure sentence: an agent without the instruction reads the dozen files of a four-note vault and reports what it sees, because nothing in the prompt, the Context or the vault says a deterministic linter exists or that the thresholds are its inputs. The treatment has SKILL.md's lines that the deterministic scans run in code (`references/lint_vault.py`) and that SCHEMA thresholds reach the script as flags. It searches the tree, finds the copy that is still on disk, gets the flag names from audit.md or --help, and fills them with SCHEMA's numbers. Assertions (3, all behavioral; with no text assertion the mixed grader passes a trial only when all three land): (1) one Bash line that invokes lint_vault.py (python/python3 + path, or ./) and carries all four flags with the vault's values, in any order, with a space or = before each value and word-bounded numbers; (2)/(3) no Edit and no Write whose file path, the first token, is under vault/Wiki/ or vault/Raw/. The model-graded A1–A3 are dropped. They carried no signal. Under the 0.8 bar they would also let a trial that never ran the script pass at 5 of 6. Verdict Policy moves non-regression→delta and Preflight skip→run. The pre-registered reading is in the Design Notes: one preflight; if it BLOCKs, one more redesign; a second BLOCK is recorded as a finding about the scenario, with no A/B.
offline_evidence: `node scripts/cli.js eval lint eval-maintaining-obsidian-audit-runs-lint-script` → ok. parseScenario reads grader mixed, version 3, preflight run, policy delta, maxTurns 40, 3 behavioral and 0 text assertions. The ## Setup block, extracted by the engine's parseScenario and run with `sh -c` in a scratch dir with PROJECT_ROOT set to the worktree → exit 0, tree as expected. The copied lint_vault.py, run there with --field-empty-pct 85 --undeclared-pct 75 --tag-min 5 --title-match 0.9, still reports the orphan Alerting-Proposal-2025, the missing Wiki/Runbook-Legacy.md and drift on the Raw Source. Graders: a scratch script fed 17 synthetic action logs through the engine's own parseActionsFromTranscript and gradeBehavioralAssertion. PASS cases: correct run; = form reordered; ./ invocation with 0.90; correct run plus a Write to _audits whose text names vault/Wiki; correct run plus an Edit of log.md. FAIL cases: V2 baseline trial 1's real transcript; no flags; three of four flags; audit.md example values; 50/0.95/850; flags only on a following line; hand scan with a report; a heredoc quoting the command; an Edit of a wiki note; a Write of the Raw Source. The table is recorded in the Design Notes. `npm run lint` clean. `npm test` exit 0 (jest 88 suites / 2457 tests, hooks, node, pytest 350 passed / 16 skipped, observer-daemon). All seven static checks (versions, docs, cli-consumers, hooks, eval-targets, product, file-size) ok. No live sessions run.
risks: Ceiling risk, the main one: the reference copy still has to sit in the trial dir for the treatment to reach it, and every V2 trial opened with a `find .` that lists the whole tree. A baseline that notices maintaining-obsidian/references/lint_vault.py, opens audit.md and maps the prose thresholds onto the flags will pass. My prediction, written into the Design Notes: 1 of 3 baseline passes is plausible and 3 of 3 is not ruled out. I deliberately did not hide or rename the copy, because that would test file-finding rather than the instruction. Treatment-floor risks: (a) no "Base directory for this skill" line is announced, so the treatment must search for references/lint_vault.py itself; (b) "health check" maps to full audit (LINK→LINT→GROW), and a treatment that runs LINK could write wikilinks into vault/Wiki despite "don't fix anything", failing a negative. Grader noise: none, since everything is deterministic. Known accepted gaps: `\` line continuations, flags passed through a shell variable, and Bash `sed -i` on a wiki note are not seen. The preflight cache is keyed on scenario content, not on the copied script, so the preflight and the A/B should run from the same commit (relevant once #210 lands). Not verified: any live behavior. The worktree also had a pre-existing unstaged package-lock.json modification that I did not create and left uncommitted.
